article.headline: Scores from last Night: Ripley stays unbeaten; South Pontotoc girls reach 6–0
article.html:
Ripley’s boys kept their unbeaten start intact with a narrow win over Center Hill, while South Pontotoc’s girls reached 6–0 on a Thursday filled with basketball sweeps and soccer shutouts. The Tigers won 54–51 and their girls added a 62–53 victory; the Cougars beat Lafayette 62–42 in girls basketball.

Pontotoc and North Pontotoc also won both ends of their basketball doubleheaders. Below are selected verified finals from November 19, 2026, with postgame records where the completed matchup reports provide them.

Ripley stays perfect as Tigers sweep Center Hill

Ripley’s boys held off Center Hill 54–51 at home, improving to 4–0 and handing the Mustangs their first loss. Center Hill left at 4–1. The close nonconference result kept the Tigers unbeaten while ending a perfect opening for the visitors.

The girls’ game also went to Ripley, 62–53 over Center Hill. The Tigers are listed at 4–1 after the victory, with Center Hill at 3–2. Together, the results gave Ripley a varsity basketball sweep on its home floor.

Pontotoc County teams sweep three doubleheaders

South Pontotoc’s girls beat Lafayette 62–42 to remain unbeaten at 6–0; Lafayette is 2–4. The Cougar boys followed with a 66–54 victory, leaving them at 4–2 and Lafayette at 2–3. Both victories came at South Pontotoc, giving the home teams a clean sweep.

Pontotoc won the girls’ game at Tupelo 57–40 and took the boys’ game 59–54. The Warriors’ girls are listed at 4–1 and their boys at 3–1 after the road wins. Tupelo’s completed matchup pages list both Golden Wave basketball teams at 1–2.

North Pontotoc completed the county’s run of basketball sweeps at Water Valley. The Viking girls won 51–26 to reach 6–2, while the boys won 53–48 and are listed at 6–1. Water Valley fell to 1–2 in girls basketball and 0–4 in boys basketball.

Close boys finishes at Hernando, Petal and Choctaw Central

Hernando’s boys edged Lake Cormorant 55–54 to move to 6–1, with the Gators at 3–3. Lake Cormorant won the girls’ game 36–30, reaching 4–1 while Hernando fell to 1–4. The split produced one of the closest basketball finishes in this selection.

St. Stanislaus also protected an unbeaten record on the road, beating Petal 61–59. The Rock-a-Chaws are listed at 5–0 after the nonconference victory; Petal is 2–4.

Brandon and Biloxi split their basketball doubleheader. Biloxi’s girls won 60–43 and remain unbeaten at 5–0, while Brandon’s girls are 5–2. Brandon’s boys won 55–41, reaching 6–1 with Biloxi at 2–2.

Neshoba Central and Choctaw Central split as well. Neshoba Central’s girls won 57–52, leaving the Rockets at 4–2 and Choctaw Central at 3–4. Choctaw Central’s boys answered with a 59–58 win and are listed at 4–1; Neshoba Central is 4–3.

Tupelo Christian Prep breaks away in girls soccer

Tupelo Christian Prep beat South Pontotoc 9–2 in Belden, with both teams listed at 3–3 afterward. The Eagles built a 6–0 halftime lead and added three goals after the break. South Pontotoc scored both of its goals in the second half.

Soccer sweeps and an out-of-state shutout

Pontotoc shut out Strayhorn twice at home. The girls won 7–0 after leading just 1–0 at halftime and scoring six goals in the second half. The boys won 3–0. The Warriors’ completed pages list their girls at 5–1 and boys at 4–2.

New Albany beat Ripley 7–0 in boys soccer and won the girls’ match by the same score. Both Bulldog teams are listed at 6–2. The boys led 4–0 at the break and added three goals in the second half; Ripley’s boys are 1–2 and girls 0–3.

Oxford swept its soccer visit to Center Hill, winning the girls’ match 7–1 and the boys’ match 2–1. The Charger girls are listed at 5–1 and boys at 4–1–1. Center Hill’s girls are 2–4 and boys 4–3 following the matches.

Lake Cormorant kept Cleveland Central off the scoreboard in both soccer matches. The girls won 3–0 and are listed at 2–5–1; the boys won 4–0 and are 5–3. Cleveland Central’s updated records are 3–3–3 for the girls and 2–9 for the boys.

Tupelo’s girls won 3–0 at South Walton in Florida, moving to 4–1. South Walton is listed at 1–4 after the nonconference match. The road shutout gave the Golden Wave a winning result outside Mississippi on a night with several home-state soccer sweeps.

For the previous afternoon’s selected matchups, see the November 19 Games To Watch preview. This recap includes only completed results that could be verified; it is not a complete statewide scoreboard.
